Let each large square have side length \(1\), so its area is \(1\).

### Figure I
The diamond joins the midpoints of the outer square, so its area is
\[
\frac12.
\]
The inner square joins the midpoints of the diamond’s sides. The midpoint quadrilateral has half the area of the original quadrilateral, so the inner square has area
\[
\frac12\left(\frac12\right)=\frac14.
\]
Thus the shaded area is
\[
S_I=\frac12-\frac14=\frac14.
\]

### Figure II
Using coordinates for the outer square, the triangle’s vertices are
\[
(0,0),\quad \left(\frac12,1\right),\quad \left(1,\frac12\right).
\]
Its area is
\[
S_{II}=\frac12\left|\frac12\cdot\frac12-1\cdot1\right|
=\frac38.
\]

### Figure III
This triangle has base \(1\) and height \(\frac12\), so
\[
S_{III}=\frac12(1)\left(\frac12\right)=\frac14.
\]

Therefore,
\[
\boxed{\text{D: }S_I=S_{III}<S_{II}}.
\]
